typography.headings: System Sans-Serif, bold, minimum 24px for extreme legibility.
typography.body: System Sans-Serif, minimum 18px. Plain language only.
typography.strategy: Soft Utility pairing. Clean, hyper-readable, designed for panic or high-stress situations. Zero visual clutter.

visual_enhancers.surfaces: Flat Solid surfaces ONLY. Use high contrast borders for separation.
visual_enhancers.corners: Soft 12px radius for standard elements, pill-shaped for major CTAs.
visual_enhancers.controls: Minimum 60dp height for ALL touchable controls (buttons, inputs) for maximal motor accessibility under stress.

components.name: I Feel Unwell Entry
components.description: Massive, high-contrast entry point button for 'I feel unwell' on the Home screen and inside the existing Call popup. Triggers the Offline SOS Screen.

components.name: Offline SOS Screen
components.description: A dedicated offline-first emergency screen. Features massive touch targets for: 'Call Caregiver', 'Call Doctor', and 'Call 112' (or configured emergency number).

components.name: Medical Card ('Show this to a helper')
components.description: A visually distinct card on the SOS Screen displaying user-approved identity, blood group, allergies, conditions, medicines (from saved list), emergency contacts, and preferred language. Read-only here.

components.name: Settings (Medical & Emergency)
components.description: Settings screen extensions to edit Medical Card fields (Name, DOB, Blood Group, Allergies, Conditions, Language) and the Emergency Country Number (default 112).

components.name: Location Share Button
components.description: A distinct button in the SOS Screen to 'Share Location'. Request precise foreground location ONLY upon tap, then opens native device Share Sheet with a Google Maps link and short SOS message. NO background tracking.

components.name: Arrival Check-In Flow
components.description: A flow to set destination and expected arrival. Uses local notification to prompt 'confirm safe'. If overdue and app is reopened, shows 'Contact caregiver' prompt. NO automatic background messaging.

components.name: HealthSheet
components.description: A generic Bottom Sheet component used for popups (e.g., the Call popup, Check-in prompts). Must maintain 60dp touch targets.

grids_and_layouts.strategy: Mobile-first flexbox layouts using React Native StyleSheet. Single column vertical stacks. Minimum 24px padding around critical buttons. Generous spacing (minimum 16px between elements). NO complex grids.

motion.strategy: Minimal motion. Basic slide-up for HealthSheet and standard React Native navigation transitions. Fade-in for location share loading states.

accessibility.contrast: Ensure all text passes WCAG AAA (minimum 7:1) for critical emergency text.
accessibility.touch_targets: Strict 60dp minimum height and width for all interactable elements.
accessibility.test_ids: Mandatory data-testid on all interactive elements (e.g., data-testid='i-feel-unwell-button'). Also use testID where React Native specifically requires it.
accessibility.language: Use absolute plain language. No jargon. No diagnosis. No emojis.

icons_and_media.strategy: Use lucide-react-native for universal iconography. NO emojis.

instructions_to_main_agent: Build purely using React Native components and StyleSheet. NO web-only components (e.g., div, span).
Add a massive 'I feel unwell' button on the Home screen and the existing Call popup.
Create the 'Offline SOS Screen' containing the 'Show this to a helper' Medical Card and extreme-sized buttons for Caregiver, Doctor, and Emergency Number (112).
The Medical Card must display: Full Name, DOB, Blood Group, Allergies, Conditions, Language, and saved MedicPal medicines.
Update Settings to allow editing of the Medical Card fields and the Emergency Number.
Implement the Location Share button: request Foreground Location ONLY when tapped, grab coords, generate Google Maps link, and open `Share.share()` native sheet with a short SOS message.

Implement the optional Check-in feature: allow setting a destination/time, schedule a local push notification. When the app is reopened and time is overdue, present a HealthSheet to 'Contact caregiver'. NEVER send automatic background messages.
Ensure the app makes absolutely zero medical inferences or diagnoses. Present user data exactly as entered.
Ensure offline support: The SOS Screen and Medical Card must render perfectly without network connectivity.
Apply `data-testid` attributes to every actionable element to satisfy system requirements. Use `testID` concurrently if necessary.
Ensure all instructions are applied for .js files as the environment uses JS.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: Prioritize emergency usability above all aesthetic trends. Clarity > Creativity in this specific context.
Do not use generic centered layouts for data; use left-aligned, highly readable lists for the Medical Card.
Maintain the MedicPal light-blue style. Do not introduce harsh, unrelated colors.
Use flat solid colors for health apps (no glassmorphism).
Never use AI assistant Emoji characters.
Ensure all interactive elements have visible touch feedback (e.g., TouchableOpacity activeOpacity).
